_comment: Freshness budgets for what is published to npm. Checked by
scripts/check_npm_publish_freshness.py, run daily by .github/workflows/npm-publish-freshness.yml.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS: #7491. npm served a month-old `latest` while the fix users
were hitting had been on `main` for weeks. Every gate in the repo was green,
because every gate measures `main` -- and `main` is not what `npm install`
gives you. A user found it from the outside and filed a bug.
max_unpublished_age_days is counted ONLY while this checkout is ahead of the
published version, so a quiet week with nothing to release is not a failure.
It is the primary signal: it is what would have caught #7491 on day 15.
max_version_distance is a backstop, not a release-cadence rule. Every merge to
`main` bumps the workspace patch, so the distance is a commit count wearing a
version number -- at the merge rate measured in #7856 (10-58 a day) 500 patches
is roughly one to seven weeks. It exists to catch a sprint that outruns the age
budget, which is why it is not tuned tight enough to fire on a normal week: a
budget that goes red every week gets muted, and a muted gate is gone.
`anchor` marks the launcher. npm/perry/package.json.tmpl pins its
optionalDependencies to its own exact version, so every other package here must
publish the SAME `latest` -- that invariant is checked with no budget at all,
because a partial publish breaks installs while both halves sit inside theirs.
Every package published from npm/ must appear here; the checker fails if the two
sets differ, so adding a platform target cannot silently shrink the gate.

packages.name: @perryts/perry
packages.why: The launcher -- the package `npm install @perryts/perry` resolves. This is the one #7491 was about.
